tells.1: Flat, stripped-down phrasing with repetitive sentence openings ('Stepwise is free to download. Stepwise Premium costs...') and no hook. It reads like a mechanical de-AI pass.
tells.2: Vague upsell filler: 'to get more of what the app has to offer' says nothing about what Premium includes.
tells.3: Specifics that appear in no other version (exactly 312 exercises, the Gwen Harper testimonial, PT-built custom programs). They read as human but may be invented.
tells.4: Stacked marketing stock phrases ('guidance you can trust,' 'so you always know,' 'keep your recovery moving,' 'unlock more of what the app has to offer').

reason: Version 3 has the most human voice and the strongest hook, but its added count, testimonial and Premium feature can't be verified, which is a real credibility and App Store risk for a health app. Version 2 is warm, clear and accurate, so it's the safest to publish once its vague Premium line is replaced with real features.
